applicability_predicate: Any threshold check whose comparison operand can become undefined or NaN, where the language's comparison semantics turn 'no value' into 'not over the limit'. The predicate is: an unconfigurable-looking parameter takes a value that makes the check unable to fail.
counterexample: percentile: 100 is legitimately the maximum and must not be treated as out of range.
maps_to_existing_operator: none. evalmut has a `vacuous` hole KIND but no parameter-range operator.
not_applicable_cases: checks that validate their parameters before comparing
languages where comparison against a null value raises rather than returning false

pair.clean_input: percentile: 95 over a normal duration distribution
pair.expected_on_clean: Verdict determined by the real p95 duration.
pair.expected_on_defective: FAIL or ERROR, naming the bad parameter. Silently passing is the defect.

risks.false_negative: An operator that only tries 150 misses negative percentiles and non-numeric values, which reach the same undefined state by another route.
risks.false_positive: Flagging boundary values (0, 100) that the check is right to accept.

semantic: `trace-span-duration` never validated its `percentile`. A value of 150 indexed past the end of the sorted durations, `calculatePercentile` returned undefined, and `undefined > max` is false, so the assertion PASSED and reported '(undefinedms) is within...'.
title: out-of-range percentile made trace-span-duration silently pass
